title: SBI Feedback Model
prompt:
Act as a leadership development coach.
Situation I need to give feedback on:
[DESCRIBE WHAT HAPPENED - THE CONTEXT AND BEHAVIOUR]
Format this as a clean SBI feedback statement:
SITUATION     :  When and where exactly did this happen? Be specific - meeting, call, 
                             report, date.
BEHAVIOUR   :  What specifically did I observe? Observable actions only, no 
                             interpretation.
IMPACT           :  What effect did this have? On me, on the team, on the outcome.
Then write 2 follow-up questions I should ask after delivering the SBI to open a dialogue.
Finally             :  rewrite the same feedback as it would typically be delivered badly,
so I can see the difference.
SBI Feedback Model
Situation Behaviour Impact
1 2 3
In Tuesday's client call... You interrupted the It made them feel unheard 
 client twice and reduced trust
PRO TIP
The most powerful part of SBI is what comes after the pause. Deliver the Impact
statement and stop talking. Most leaders fill the silence with justifications or softening
language that undoes the feedback. Let the person respond to what they heard. Their
response tells you everything about whether the feedback landed.
